caveats: This is a structured case study, not a statistically validated causal finding. One company over one date range yields too few distinct incidents for the sentiment/abnormal-return relationship to carry statistical significance; a proper event study spans dozens of companies and events.
Flagged days are days on which unusual coverage COINCIDED WITH an unusual benchmark-adjusted return. Coincidence in time is not evidence that an article caused a price move.

2 flagged day(s) show a price move in the opposite direction to the coverage's tone. That is not necessarily an error: news can be already priced in, or the day's move driven by something the coverage did not capture.

sentiment_return_correlation.note: Pearson r over 54 news-carrying day(s) in this run; descriptive only, not a significance test, and not comparable across runs with different day counts.

sentiment_extremity_volume_correlation.note: Pearson r over 54 news-carrying day(s) between |sentiment| and volume's own z-score; descriptive only, not a significance test.

1.note: Pearson r over 54 pair(s) of (day t sentiment, day t+1 abnormal return); descriptive only, not a significance test.

5.note: Pearson r over 54 pair(s) of (day t sentiment, day t+5 abnormal return); descriptive only, not a significance test.

emotion_return_summary.note: 20 day(s) had a confident dominant emotion (GoEmotions, headline-only, secondary to FinBERT); grouped by the paper's own positive/negative/ambiguous clustering. Descriptive only — small day counts per group, and this never affects incident flagging or ranking.

threshold_robustness.note: each candidate day's flagging test re-run across 9 combinations of coverage/return z-thresholds (0.7x/1x/1.3x of the 1/1.5 configured values). A day flagged in all combinations is robust to the exact threshold chosen; one flagged in only the loosest combination is threshold-sensitive - treat it with more caution.

sectors.narrative: Refinery throughput supported by robust domestic fuel consumption and export margins.
Peak summer power demand and industrial baseload driving record thermal and renewable generation.
Infrastructure capex, railway modernization, and automotive demand underpinning crude steel output.

Offshore aging field declines offset by deepwater KG-basin production ramping.
City gas distribution networks (CGD) and fertilizer feedstock demand maintaining positive momentum.
Highway construction, affordable housing projects, and commercial real estate buildout driving dispatches.
Kharif sowing season buffer stocking and domestic urea/DAP production plants running at full capacity.
